status_effects.explanation: Gilberte's report casts Albertine as a mildly disreputable, odd figure, a small local diminishment relative to Gilberte's own poised judgment.
Swann's emphatic praise locally elevates Mme Bontemps despite Gilberte's dislike, though the praise's value is undercut by the surrounding critique of Swann's own diminished discourse.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Elle sera sûrement très « fast » mais en attendant elle a une drôle de touche. » / « Je ne la connais pas. Je la voyais seulement passer, on criait Albertine par-ci, Albertine par-là. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Gilberte offhandedly characterizes Albertine as odd-looking and predicts she will become socially 'fast,' a mild dismissive judgment reported without narratorial endorsement or irony.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Tu as le plus grand tort, elle est charmante, jolie, intelligente. Elle est même spirituelle. » — overriding Gilberte's « je connais Mme Bontemps, et elle ne me plaît pas non plus. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Swann enthusiastically praises Mme Bontemps and overrules his daughter's stated dislike of her, but this praise occurs within the very speech the narrator elsewhere frames as symptomatic of Swann's decline into banal, socially eager talk, leaving its sincerity uncertain.
